memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'when they sin in any of these ways and realise their guilt, they must return what they have stolen or taken by extortion, or what was entrusted to them, or the lost property they found,'" - Lev 6:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They must return it. Not feel sorry about it. Not pray about it. Return it.

God's forgiveness has never been the enemy of practical action. In fact it produces it. A man who has genuinely met God's mercy finds that the stolen item starts to burn a hole in his house.

Notice the range of things listed: stolen goods, extorted money, an entrusted deposit, lost property kept quietly. God covers every way we can end up holding something that is not ours — from outright theft to simply never getting around to giving it back.

That last category catches most of us. Not dramatic dishonesty, just things we borrowed and kept, credit we accepted for someone else's work, money we owe that nobody has chased.

Jesus made this a priority even over worship: if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there... First go and be reconciled (Mtt 5:23-24). He put the relationship ahead of the ritual.

Is there something in your possession, or on your conscience, that belongs to someone else?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something I am holding — money, credit, an object — that is not really mine?
2. What one practical step could I take this week to return it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not want to hold anything that belongs to another. Show me what to return, and give me the humility to do it. Amen.
